$schema_note: Tuned numbers for the retinue economy. Decisions + rationale live in SYSTEMS.md §7 and docs/design/retinue-economy.md (task-101 reconciliation). All values are PROTOTYPE DIALS (first pass) to be re-tuned in play, not committed balance.

supply.note: Supply is CAPACITY (headroom), not a draining stock. Upkeep DEMAND = sum of per-unit upkeep. Units degrade when demand > capacity; they NEVER die from upkeep (GDD §7). Provision raises capacity; recruiting raises demand. start_capacity=120 matches the GATE1 refill-to-cap retinue convention (docs/GATE1-FUN-PROTOTYPE.md, docs/data/scenarios/gate1-calibration-wave1.json) so the retinue does not open the run already 2x over capacity -- see docs/design/retinue-economy.md.
supply.upkeep_note: Uniform 1/unit across tiers in the slice. This makes PROMOTE upkeep-neutral (quality lane) and RECRUIT upkeep-hungry (breadth lane) — the core of the triangle. Per-tier upkeep is a parked v2 knob.

also_applies: cannot hold formation reliably (may rout under pressure)
freshly recruited units enter degraded until capacity recovers (GDD §7)
degrade.never: death — degrade is the whole mechanic

embers.retired: RETIRED 2026-07-31 (Embers deleted) — history, not a live dial. See docs/design/DIRECTION-2026-07-31.md.
embers.note: Embers are the SPEND currency for the RECRUIT / PROMOTE / PROVISION triangle and for items / hero nodes. Tuned so a player reaches each growth site with ~30-40 Embers — enough for 2-3 actions, never all of them. Scarcity IS the decision.

income.veteran_survives_wave_note: 0 by default; the 'oath_ledger' item turns this on (+2) — an economy-engine item, not a baseline.

scaling_curve.note: One curve across the slice's 3 waves — the first act of the exponential fantasy (RTS-VERTICAL-SLICE §4). Brood counts are the gate-1 values; the economy must let a well-played run keep pace.

slice_targets.design_intent: Gate-1 zero-input baseline LOSES wave 3 by 4-13 brood (docs/GATE1-FUN-PROTOTYPE.md §3). The economy layer must be the margin: played well it turns the narrow loss into a win; hoarded or mismanaged (over-recruit past supply → a degraded, dimmed army) it turns into a blowout loss. If a single dominant allocation always wins, the triangle has failed and needs re-tuning.
